behaviour: getLassoSelectedElementIds takes an optional boxSelectionMode: "overlap" (or omitted) keeps today's enclosed-or-intersected result; "contain" mirrors box selection's contain mode: an element qualifies only when its (frame-clipped) outline is fully inside the lasso and no lasso edge cuts it, and a group qualifies only when every member qualifies.
rules: 1. Add `boxSelectionMode?: BoxSelectionMode;` as the last field of the input object type (after simplifyDistance) and destructure it as `boxSelectionMode = "overlap"`.

2. Keep the path simplification, the unlockedElements filter, the clearing of both sets, the lassoBounds reduce and the doBoundsIntersect / not-already-in-a-set guard exactly as they are, for both modes.
3. In the loop, when boxSelectionMode === "contain" and isBoundToContainer(element) is true, `continue` before the bounds guard.

4. Inside the guarded block, when boxSelectionMode === "contain": const frame = getContainingFrame(element, elementsMap); const clipBounds = frame && elementOverlapsWithFrame(element, frame, elementsMap) ? getElementBounds(frame, elementsMap) : null; add element.id to enclosedElements only when fullEnclosureTest(path, element, elementsSegments, clipBounds) is true and then intersectionTest(path, element, elementsMap, clipBounds) is false (call intersectionTest only after fullEnclosureTest passed). Never add to intersectedElements in this branch.
5. Otherwise (overlap) keep today's branch unchanged: enclosureTest first, then intersectionTest(path, element, elementsMap) only when not enclosed.

6. After the loop, when boxSelectionMode === "contain": collect the top-level group ids `elementsMap.get(id)?.groupIds.at(-1)` of the enclosed ids into a Set (skip undefined); when that Set is empty do nothing more. Otherwise mark a group as failing when some element of elementsMap.values() with !isDeleted, !locked and !isBoundToContainer has that top-level group id and is not in enclosedElements; then delete from enclosedElements every id whose element's groupIds.at(-1) is a failing group. Iterate a copy (`[...enclosedElements]`) when deleting.
7. Return { selectedElementIds: [...intersectedElements, ...enclosedElements] } as today.

8. Add a module-private `const fullEnclosureTest = (lassoPath: GlobalPoint[], element: ExcalidrawElement, elementsSegments: ElementsSegmentsMap, clipBounds: Bounds | null): boolean` placed right after enclosureTest: build the polygon once with polygonFromPoints(lassoPath); return false when the element has no segments entry or an empty one; otherwise return segments.every(segment => segment.every(point => polygonIncludesPointNonZero(p, lassoPolygon))) where p is the point itself when clipBounds is null, else pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(Math.min(Math.max(point[0], clipBounds[0]), clipBounds[2]), Math.min(Math.max(point[1], clipBounds[1]), clipBounds[3])).

9. intersectionTest gains a fourth parameter `clipBounds: Bounds | null = null`. When it is null the function body behaves exactly as today (onlyFirst true, `.length > 0`). When it is set, both intersectElementWithLineSegment calls (element and bound text) pass onlyFirst false and count as a hit only when the returned points `.some((point) => pointInsideBounds(point, clipBounds))` (pointInsideBounds(p, bounds: Bounds): boolean is the strict check exported by @excalidraw/element). Keep the lassoSegments construction and the bound-text positioning as they are.

10. Add `pointFrom` to the @excalidraw/math named import; add `elementOverlapsWithFrame`, `getContainingFrame`, `isBoundToContainer` and `pointInsideBounds` to the existing named import from "@excalidraw/element"; add `import type { BoxSelectionMode } from "../types";` as the last import, after a blank line.
11. Do not change enclosureTest.

behaviour: Pins every existing lasso case to overlap mode and adds unit-level coverage of both modes for each shape kind, the omitted-mode default, bound-text labels, frames (including a child protruding from its frame), groups and a concave lasso cutting an element.
rules: 1. Imports: replace the `./test-utils` import line with `import { API } from "./helpers/api";`, a blank line, the unchanged `import { act, render } from "./test-utils";`, a blank line, and `import type { BoxSelectionMode } from "../types";` (type import last).

2. updatePath gains a required third parameter `boxSelectionMode: BoxSelectionMode`; its first statement is `API.setAppState({ boxSelectionMode });` (outside the existing act), and the direct getLassoSelectedElementIds call passes `boxSelectionMode` as its last field. Everything else in updatePath stays as it is.
3. Every existing `updatePath(startPoint, points);` call becomes `updatePath(startPoint, points, "overlap");`; no existing assertion changes.

4. Append one top-level `describe("lasso box selection mode", ...)` after the last describe. Its beforeEach sets the lasso tool inside act (`h.app.setActiveTool({ type: "lasso" })`); the file-level beforeEach already renders.

5. Inside it define `squareLasso = (x: number, y: number, size: number)` returning `{ startPoint: pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(x, y), points: [[0, 0], [size, 0], [size, size], [0, size], [0, 0]] as LocalPoint[] }`, and two constants: ENCLOSING = squareLasso(-50, -50, 200) and TOUCHING = squareLasso(60, 60, 200).

6. Define `shapes` as an array of `[label, () => ExcalidrawElement]` tuples, each factory calling API.createElement with a literal type: rectangle {x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100}; ellipse same box; diamond same box; "rotated rectangle" {type: "rectangle", x: 20, y: 20, width: 60, height: 60, angle: Math.PI / 4}; line {x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100, points: [pointFrom<LocalPoint>(0, 0), pointFrom<LocalPoint>(100, 100)]}; arrow with the same props; freedraw {x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100, points: [pointFrom<LocalPoint>(0, 0), pointFrom<LocalPoint>(50, 20), pointFrom<LocalPoint>(100, 100)]}.

7. Shape cases use it.each(shapes) with a `%s` title; each creates the element, calls API.setElements([element]), runs updatePath with the lasso's startPoint and points and the mode, and asserts the selected ids with getSelectedElements(h.elements, h.state).map(e => e.id).

8. The omitted-mode case calls getLassoSelectedElementIds directly (no updatePath): lassoPath is the TOUCHING square as five GlobalPoints (60,60), (260,60), (260,260), (60,260), (60,60); elementsSegments is built with getElementLineSegments over h.elements as updatePath does; fresh Sets are passed on every call.

9. The bound-text case uses API.createTextContainer(), API.setElements on both returned elements, reads the label from the scene with API.getElement(label), and lassos a square from (label.x - 5, label.y - 5) with size Math.max(label.width, label.height) + 10.

10. The frame cases create a frame with API.createElement({ type: "frame", x: 0, y: 0, width: 400, height: 400 }) and a child rectangle {x: 50, y: 50, width: 100, height: 100, frameId: frame.id}; the child-only lasso is squareLasso(25, 25, 150) and the whole-frame lasso is squareLasso(-50, -50, 500).

11. The protruding-child case creates a frame {type: "frame", x: 0, y: 0, width: 200, height: 200} and a child rectangle {x: 150, y: 50, width: 100, height: 100, frameId: frame.id} (its right half lies outside the frame), and lassos the visible part with startPoint pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(140, 40) and points [[0, 0], [70, 0], [70, 120], [0, 120], [0, 0]] as LocalPoint[].

12. The group cases create rectA {type: "rectangle", x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100, groupIds: ["g1"]} and rectB the same at x: 300; the one-member lasso is ENCLOSING (encloses rectA only) and the whole-group lasso is squareLasso(-50, -50, 500).

13. The concave case creates a rectangle {x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100} and a lasso with startPoint pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(-50, -50) and points [[0, 0], [90, 0], [100, 100], [110, 0], [200, 0], [200, 200], [0, 200], [0, 0]] as LocalPoint[]: all four corners lie inside the polygon while the notch reaching (50, 50) cuts the rectangle's top edge.

rules: 1. The "lasso reselection" beforeEach renders `<Excalidraw initialData={{ appState: { boxSelectionMode: "overlap" } }} />` instead of `<Excalidraw />`; its test body is unchanged.

2. Add a top-level `describe("lasso box selection mode", ...)` right after the "lasso reselection" describe. Inside it define `lassoSelect = (points: [number, number][])`: act(() => h.app.setActiveTool({ type: "lasso" })), mouse.downAt on the first point, mouse.moveTo on each remaining point, then mouse.up().

3. Scene for every case: rect1 = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 0, y: 0, width: 50, height: 50, backgroundColor: "red", fillStyle: "solid" }) and rect2 the same at x: 100; API.setElements([rect1, rect2]).
4. The lasso for every case is lassoSelect([[-20, -20], [125, -20], [125, 70], [-20, 70], [-20, -20]]): rect1 is fully enclosed, rect2 is only partially covered.

6. The preference-change case lives in the wrap describe and calls API.setAppState({ boxSelectionMode: "overlap" }) before lassoSelect.

behaviour: Records under Unreleased that the lasso now honours the Wrap/Overlap box selection preference and that the default (Wrap) lasso is enclose-only.
rules: 1. Insert, after the last Breaking changes bullet of the Unreleased `## Excalidraw Library` section: a blank line, `### Behavior changes`, a blank line, and one bullet.

2. The bullet says: the lasso tool now follows the box selection mode preference (`appState.boxSelectionMode`); in the default Wrap (`"contain"`) mode it selects only elements it fully encloses, matching box selection (a group only when all its members are enclosed, a frame child by its part visible inside the frame), while Overlap (`"overlap"`) mode keeps the previous behavior of also selecting elements the lasso path touches; it ends with `[#11809](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/11809)`.

3. Mention that `getLassoSelectedElementIds` is unaffected for callers that omit the new optional `boxSelectionMode` input only if it fits in the same bullet as one short clause; add no other bullets.
